NUTRITION
  GUIDELINES:
    - "Energy: aim for slight maintenance to small surplus (~+100-250 kcal) on heavy training days; maintain on light days; on planned fat-loss phases aim for modest deficit but avoid large deficits which can worsen vasomotor symptoms."
    - "Protein: 1.2..1.6 g/kg bodyweight daily (priority for muscle and bone maintenance)."
    - "Calcium: ensure ~1000-1200 mg/day through dairy or fortified alternatives."
    - "Vitamin D: ensure adequate status; supplement per GP if low (common in perimenopause)."
    - "Healthy fats: include sources of omega-3s (e.g., fatty fish) to support inflammation and cardiovascular health."
    - "Phytoestrogens: include soy, flaxseed, legumes regularly to potentially ease vasomotor symptoms."
    - "Hydration & cooling: drink cool fluids before/during/after cardio and training; use cooling strategies (cold towel, fan) post-session to reduce hot-flash risk."
    - "Caffeine & alcohol: limit close to bedtime and around evening training; moderate overall as they can trigger vasomotor symptoms."
    - "Meal timing: avoid fasted high-intensity cardio in heat; schedule aerobic intervals and harder sessions earlier in day or in cool environment."
    - "Fiber-rich carbohydrates: prioritize whole grains, fruits, vegetables for gut health and stable energy."
    - "Sodium & electrolytes: consider modest electrolyte intake during long aerobic sessions or when sweating heavily."
    - "Fasted HIIT safety: only include short, low-heat fasted HIIT sessions (≤20m total) on low-humidity, cool mornings; monitor symptoms closely and stop if dizziness, excessive hot flashes, or palpitations occur."

    DAY "Training Heavy":
      - "Breakfast: whole-grain porridge with milk/fortified plant milk, tablespoon ground flaxseed, handful berries, 20-30 g whey or plant protein."
      - "Lunch: mixed salad with leafy greens, 120-150 g fatty fish or tofu, quinoa, avocado, olive oil dressing."
      - "Snack: yogurt or fortified alternative + fruit + 10-15 g mixed nuts."
      - "Dinner: lean protein (chicken, fish, legumes), steamed vegetables, sweet potato or brown rice."
      - "Supplement: calcium + vitamin D if advised by GP; consider omega-3 supplement."
    DAY "Training Light / Rest":
      - "Breakfast: Greek yogurt or fortified alternative with fruit and oats; sprinkle chia/flax."
      - "Lunch: lentil or bean-based soup, whole-grain bread, side salad."
      - "Snack: apple + nut butter."
      - "Dinner: salmon or tempeh, broccoli, whole grain."
    DAY "Aerobic Long":
      - "Pre-session: small carbohydrate snack and cool fluid 30-60m prior (banana, toast)."
      - "During: cool water; for >60m consider electrolyte drink."
      - "Post-session: protein + carbohydrate within 2 hours (protein shake + banana or sandwich)."
    DAY "Fasted HIIT Morning":
      - "Guidance: keep sessions ≤20 minutes, in a cool environment, low humidity; consume cool fluids before; if any vasomotor symptoms worsen stop session."
      - "Example: 15m cycling intervals (30s hard / 90s easy) done fasted in cool morning, followed immediately by 10-20 g protein and cool fluid."

MONITORING
  - "Track symptoms (hot flashes frequency/intensity) and adjust timing/environment of sessions; reduce/stop fasted HIIT if symptoms increase."
  - "Review calcium & vitamin D intake with GP; consider blood test for vitamin D."
  - "Adjust calories based on weight and recovery (fatigue, sleep)."

SAFETY
  - "Avoid sauna and exercising in very hot environments; prefer indoor cooled sessions when vasomotor symptoms are significant."
  - "No fasted high-intensity cardio in heat; fasted HIIT only in cool, low-humidity mornings and kept short as above."
  - "Use structured cooling post-session (cool shower, cold towel, fan) to mitigate hot flashes."
  - "Stop any fasted HIIT immediately if dizziness, faintness, palpitations, or severe hot flashes occur and seek medical advice if needed."

VISITS
  CHECKINS:
    - "Week 4: review progress, symptoms, and nutrition adherence."
    - "Week 8: strength test and symptom review; adjust calories if needed."
    - "Week 12: final assessment and next-phase planning; perform 1RM testing for squat, bench_press, and deadlift in a cooled environment with full warm-up and spotter present."

NUTRITION
  GUIDELINES:
    - "Energy: aim for slight maintenance to small surplus (~+100-250 kcal) on heavy training days; maintain on light days; on planned fat-loss phases aim for modest deficit but avoid large deficits which can worsen vasomotor symptoms."
    - "Protein: 1.2..1.6 g/kg bodyweight daily (priority for muscle and bone maintenance)."
    - "Calcium: ensure ~1000-1200 mg/day through dairy or fortified alternatives."
    - "Vitamin D: ensure adequate status; supplement per GP if low (common in perimenopause)."
    - "Healthy fats: include sources of omega-3s (e.g., fatty fish) to support inflammation and cardiovascular health."
    - "Phytoestrogens: include soy, flaxseed, legumes regularly to potentially ease vasomotor symptoms."
    - "Hydration & cooling: drink cool fluids before/during/after cardio and training; use cooling strategies (cold towel, fan) post-session to reduce hot-flash risk."
    - "Caffeine & alcohol: limit close to bedtime and around evening training; moderate overall as they can trigger vasomotor symptoms."
    - "Meal timing: avoid fasted high-intensity cardio in heat; schedule aerobic intervals and harder sessions earlier in day or in cool environment."
    - "Fiber-rich carbohydrates: prioritize whole grains, fruits, vegetables for gut health and stable energy."
    - "Sodium & electrolytes: consider modest electrolyte intake during long aerobic sessions or when sweating heavily."
    - "Fasted HIIT safety: only include short, low-heat fasted HIIT sessions (≤20m total) on low-humidity, cool mornings; monitor symptoms closely and stop if dizziness, excessive hot flashes, or palpitations occur."

  SAMPLE DAILY PLANS:
    DAY "Training Heavy":
      - "Breakfast: whole-grain porridge with milk/fortified plant milk, tablespoon ground flaxseed, handful berries, 20-30 g whey or plant protein."
      - "Lunch: mixed salad with leafy greens, 120-150 g fatty fish or tofu, quinoa, avocado, olive oil dressing."
      - "Snack: yogurt or fortified alternative + fruit + 10-15 g mixed nuts."
      - "Dinner: lean protein (chicken, fish, legumes), steamed vegetables, sweet potato or brown rice."
      - "Supplement: calcium + vitamin D if advised by GP; consider omega-3 supplement."
    DAY "Training Light / Rest":
      - "Breakfast: Greek yogurt or fortified alternative with fruit and oats; sprinkle chia/flax."
      - "Lunch: lentil or bean-based soup, whole-grain bread, side salad."
      - "Snack: apple + nut butter."
      - "Dinner: salmon or tempeh, broccoli, whole grain."
    DAY "Aerobic Long":
      - "Pre-session: small carbohydrate snack and cool fluid 30-60m prior (banana, toast)."
      - "During: cool water; for >60m consider electrolyte drink."
      - "Post-session: protein + carbohydrate within 2 hours (protein shake + banana or sandwich)."
    DAY "Fasted HIIT Morning":
      - "Guidance: keep sessions ≤20 minutes, in a cool environment, low humidity; consume cool fluids before; if any vasomotor symptoms worsen stop session."
      - "Example: 15m cycling intervals (30s hard / 90s easy) done fasted in cool morning, followed immediately by 10-20 g protein and cool fluid."

MONITORING
  - "Track symptoms (hot flashes frequency/intensity) and adjust timing/environment of sessions; reduce/stop fasted HIIT if symptoms increase."
  - "Review calcium & vitamin D intake with GP; consider blood test for vitamin D."
  - "Adjust calories based on weight and recovery (fatigue, sleep)."

SAFETY
  - "Avoid sauna and exercising in very hot environments; prefer indoor cooled sessions when vasomotor symptoms are significant."
  - "No fasted high-intensity cardio in heat; fasted HIIT only in cool, low-humidity mornings and kept short as above."
  - "Use structured cooling post-session (cool shower, cold towel, fan) to mitigate hot flashes."
  - "Stop any fasted HIIT immediately if dizziness, faintness, palpitations, or severe hot flashes occur and seek medical advice if needed."

VISITS

    - "Week 8: strength test and symptom review; adjust calories if needed."
    - "Week 12: final assessment and next-phase planning; perform 1RM testing for squat, bench_press, and deadlift in a cooled environment with full warm-up and spotter present."
